so-eds.how: Sites Optimizer connects to your Edge Delivery site through its code repository and content source. With the Ultimate package, it deploys approved SEO and content fixes to the source documents or authoring, where your team reviews and publishes them.
so-eds.gain: Edge Delivery builds search in from day one. As your site grows, Sites Optimizer finds SEO and performance issues and deploys suggested fixes to authoring for your team to publish.

bv-bc.how: We map the questions Brand Visibility tracks to the approved sources and the answers Brand Concierge gives on your site. This is a working method we run between the two products, not a data feed from one to the other.
bv-bc.gain: We check that the questions buyers ask AI assistants are covered by your approved Brand Concierge sources, and we test the answers against those sources on your site.

cw-cja.how: Coworker Chat reads Customer Journey Analytics directly. The Skills we build turn your agreed AI-channel measures in a validated data view into a repeatable readout.
cw-cja.gain: A Skill we build turns your agreed AI channel measures in CJA into a repeatable readout.

cw-eds.how: Coworker updates AEM pages, including Edge Delivery pages and bulk changes across many pages, once you have Coworker and AEM agent access. Your authors review and publish each change.
cw-eds.gain: With AEM agent access in place, your content team rolls an approved change across many pages in one request, checked against your brand, and your authors publish.

cw-bc.how: Coworker queries your Brand Concierge conversation datasets in Experience Platform. The CSV download needs Data Distiller. Skills we build summarize the conversations and flag answers for your team to review.
cw-bc.gain: A Skill we build summarizes exported conversations and flags answers for a person on your team to review.

ads-cja.how: Google Ads, Pinterest, Snapchat and TikTok sources come with CJA. Adobe's connector page does not state whether the Meta Ads source is included, so if you select Meta Ads we confirm your entitlement with Adobe before this work starts. Experience Platform creates the paid media datasets itself, and ad spend joins web conversions through the campaign, ad group and ad IDs in your landing page URLs, at the aggregate level.
ads-cja.note: Adobe states no license line for the Meta Ads source; if your client selects Meta Ads, confirm the entitlement with Adobe before the work starts.

csrc-eds.how: Your authors write pages in Word or Google Docs in your SharePoint or Google Drive, and Edge Delivery publishes them as pages. This applies only when you author in documents; with Experience Workspace or AEM Sites, authoring stays in Adobe.

csrc-so.how: For eligible opportunities, Sites Optimizer writes approved fixes back into the source documents, using the route Adobe documents for that opportunity. Your authors review and publish them from Sidekick. SharePoint on your own domain needs an app registration with site write access; Google Drive needs a folder share with Editor access.

aemsites-bv.how: On AEM as a Cloud Service's managed CDN, Brand Visibility's Optimize at Edge is self-serve when that CDN is the outer CDN. If your own CDN sits in front, it needs its own routing. The AI agents Adobe supports (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude) get the optimized version of pages where a fix is deployed; visitors and search bots still get AEM's pages.
aemsites-bv.gain: Approved fixes reach the supported AI agents from AEM's CDN without changing the pages your visitors see. Content fixes need a Last-Modified header on the page, and they pause for review when the source page changes. Sampled AEM telemetry gives an approximate view of AI-referred visits, not person-level data.

aemsites-so.how: Sites Optimizer deploys approved fixes into your AEM author environment (deploying is in the Ultimate package), where your authors review and publish them. It does not publish to the live site itself, except Dispatcher redirects where Adobe has enabled them.
aemsites-so.gain: SEO and accessibility fixes land in AEM author for your authors to publish. Speed fixes can arrive as pull requests where a code repository is connected and Adobe has enabled the selected feature.

aemassets-eds.how: For Edge Delivery sites authored in AEM's Universal Editor, your authors select AEM Assets directly and the assets publish with the page. For sites authored in Word or Google Docs, a configured AEM Assets Sidekick plugin inserts assets as copies or as approved Dynamic Media with OpenAPI references. Dynamic Media references in the Universal Editor use a custom asset picker.
aemassets-eds.gain: Your authors pick assets from AEM Assets inside Word, Google Docs or the Universal Editor. With Dynamic Media references, pages stay current when assets change or expire, once block code renders the delivery URLs.

aemsites-cw.how: Where you have access to AEM's agentic capabilities, Coworker Chat works in AEM Sites. From a plain-language prompt it drafts and updates pages, on Page Editor sites as on Edge Delivery sites, builds Visual Content Fragments from Figma and helps your developers with Cloud Manager and the Dispatcher.
aemsites-cw.gain: Your content team describes a page or a change in plain words and Coworker drafts it in AEM Sites from an approved reference page for review. Your developers get AI diagnosis of build, code scan and config pipeline failures to review before acting.

aemassets-cw.how: Where you have AEM agent access, AEM's Onboarding, Content Discovery and Content Optimization capabilities work through Coworker Chat. Coworker sets up folders, tags and metadata forms once the user confirms, finds assets by metadata or theme and can filter to approved ones, and makes channel-ready renditions where you have a Dynamic Media license, Dynamic Media with OpenAPI and approved assets.
aemassets-cw.gain: Your teams find assets in plain words and set up folders, tags and metadata forms with Coworker, confirming each change first. With Dynamic Media with OpenAPI they also get channel-ready renditions of approved assets.

ajo-target.how: Manual A/B Test and Experience Targeting activities in Target can serve offer decisions built in Journey Optimizer Decision Management. We confirm Adobe's direction for this route before new offer work starts. Journey Optimizer organizations can also share audiences to Target through the separate Adobe Target destination.
ajo-target.gain: The same offer decision can serve web tests in manual A/B and Experience Targeting activities. Reporting is in Target at activity level, not in Analytics for Target, since Target gives no offer-decision level reporting.
ajo-target.note: Adobe marks offer decisions in Target and Journey Optimizer Decision Management as Legacy. Confirm Adobe's direction for this route before new offer work for your client.

ajo-bc.how: Adobe's product page describes Journey Optimizer follow-up after concierge conversations. Experience League documents no setup for it, so we confirm the route with Adobe before this work starts. The follow-up routes Adobe documents are the handoff to sales and Marketo Engage.
ajo-bc.gain: If Adobe confirms a route for you, a visitor who showed intent in a concierge conversation could get a follow-up by email, SMS or other channels. Adobe documents no setup for this, so the work waits for that confirmation.
ajo-bc.note: Not a documented capability: Experience League has no Journey Optimizer setup for Brand Concierge. Confirm with Adobe that a route exists for your client before promising follow-up journeys.

cja-bc.how: Brand Concierge's built-in analytics dashboard is powered by Customer Journey Analytics and needs no separate CJA license. Analysis alongside your other journey data uses your separately licensed CJA. Concierge events reach your CJA in one of two ways: through the bundled Concierge dataset, where Adobe confirms in writing that the dataset may be joined with your web or commerce data, or otherwise as callback events collected separately through your licensed collection route. We agree the route with you and document the dataset permissions before this work starts.
cja-bc.gain: The built-in dashboard shows conversation trends, repeat engagement, intent, sentiment, feedback and recommendations. With your separately licensed CJA, we analyze the Concierge events from the agreed and permitted collection route next to your journey and purchase data.
cja-bc.note: Settle the Concierge-bundled dataset's permitted use with Adobe in writing before reusing it in your client's CJA connection; if Adobe does not confirm it, collect concierge events through the client-side callback functions into your client's own data collection instead.

target-commerce.how: We map the agreed Commerce storefront events and attributes to supported Target parameters in your Target-enabled Web SDK implementation. Adobe documents store-content testing use cases and the generic Web SDK setup, not this specific mapping, so we validate the mapping and the end-to-end behavior on your storefront in a pilot.
target-commerce.gain: Target tests your store content and offers. Using Commerce events in Target is a design we validate in a pilot on your storefront. Product recommendations are separate work.
target-commerce.note: Adobe does not state this route; confirm it with Adobe for your client's tenant before work starts, and treat the Commerce-to-Target mapping as a design to prove in the pilot, not a documented capability.

target-eds.how: Adobe documents two ways to run Target on Edge Delivery pages: Web SDK, which Adobe recommends, and at.js, Adobe's earlier library. Adobe's martech plugin, which comes through AEM Engineering, is a third route that applies page changes as each block renders; it also needs Adobe Analytics and a Tags property. If you choose the plugin route, we confirm its availability with Adobe before this work starts.
target-eds.gain: Target tests and personalization run on your Edge Delivery pages. In Adobe's own test, plugin page modifications added 1.2 seconds to mobile Largest Contentful Paint; the route, the device and the complexity of each change affect the result, so we measure Largest Contentful Paint on your pages with the route you choose.
target-eds.note: at.js is the legacy route and the martech plugin is co-innovation from AEM Engineering's One Adobe lab; confirm the plugin's availability with Adobe before proposing it, and measure Largest Contentful Paint on your client's own pages rather than relying on Adobe's +1.2 second figure.

ajo-eds.how: Journey Optimizer web campaigns need Web SDK on your site. On Edge Delivery, aem.live describes running them through the martech plugin, from AEM Engineering's One Adobe lab, as an alternative to Target. The aem.live guide does not describe a direct Web SDK route for Journey Optimizer, so we validate that route in a pilot before this work relies on it.
ajo-eds.gain: Journey Optimizer web campaigns can change your Edge Delivery pages through the martech plugin. Adobe measured a baseline of 1.2 seconds added to mobile Largest Contentful Paint with page modifications, and complex changes add more. We measure Largest Contentful Paint on the agreed campaigns and pages.
ajo-eds.note: The martech plugin is co-innovation from AEM Engineering's One Adobe lab, and a direct Web SDK route for Journey Optimizer on Edge Delivery is a pilot item that aem.live does not describe: prove it in a pilot before promising it to your client, and measure the agreed campaigns and pages against Adobe's +1.2-second mobile LCP baseline.

rtcdp-eds.how: The martech plugin, which comes through AEM Engineering, loads Web SDK on your Edge Delivery pages. Web SDK sends site events to Experience Platform, and Experience Platform builds profiles in Profile-enabled datasets. A Tags-only Web SDK route is a separately configured implementation that we validate for your site.
rtcdp-eds.gain: What visitors do on your Edge Delivery pages lands in their profiles where consent allows, ready for audiences and activation.
rtcdp-eds.note: The martech plugin is available through AEM Engineering co-innovation, and a Tags-only Web SDK route is separately configured and must be validated for your client's site before it is counted on.

marketo-workfront.how: We build Workfront Fusion scenarios from Adobe's blueprint to link Marketo Engage and Workfront: a Workfront request form sets up a Marketo Engage program from a template, and Marketo emails come back to Workfront as proofs whose approval is sent back to Marketo Engage.
marketo-workfront.gain: Campaign requests arrive on a structured Workfront form, a Fusion scenario clones the matching Marketo program template and fills its My Tokens, and emails are proofed and approved in Workfront. Audiences are still built by a user or come from a smart list in the template.

marketo-cja.how: Marketo person and activity data comes into Experience Platform through the Marketo Engage source connector. A CJA connection and data view then make it reportable next to your web data. Adobe suggests CJA B2B Edition for more value but does not require it.
marketo-cja.gain: We validate the ID strategy and graph-based stitching (CJA Prime or higher) in a pilot. Marketo activity then sits next to web visits, so your marketers can compare program activity with later web and conversion activity. Numbers can differ from Marketo's own reports, and account and opportunity views need CJA B2B Edition.

marketo-cw.how: Coworker for Marketo Engage adds agent skills inside Marketo Engage that build programs, investigate leads, validate programs and import leads. It is enabled per subscription, and user access is set up after enablement. We confirm with Adobe that it is enabled for your subscription before this work starts.
marketo-cw.gain: Your marketers describe a campaign in plain words and Coworker builds the program structure with asset placeholders and scheduling, checks it before launch and explains why a lead stalled. Your team still writes and approves the assets.

workfront-cw.how: CX Enterprise Coworker Chat runs inside Workfront within each user's permissions. It is read-only until your Workfront system administrator turns on the Write MCP tools option. Adobe confirms that Coworker is available to your organization before this service starts.
workfront-cw.gain: Once your Workfront admin turns on write access, Coworker can carry out steps within each user's permissions and return the work for approval.
workfront-cw.note: Adobe's Coworker in Workfront overview says Coworker is not currently offered to organizations in health care, finance or some other industries with sensitive data; confirm your client's eligibility with Adobe before this work starts.

workfront-ajo.how: Workfront Fusion's Adobe Journey Optimizer modules create, read, update and delete Journey Optimizer records such as content templates and fragments, so work in Workfront can feed Journey Optimizer. This needs a Workfront Fusion license.
workfront-ajo.gain: A Fusion scenario we build can create or update Journey Optimizer content templates and fragments when work is approved in Workfront, cutting copy and paste between your teams.

aemsites-aemassets.how: Dynamic Media with OpenAPI lets your Sites authors use approved assets from a remote AEM Assets environment in the Page Editor. Remote assets in Content Fragments work on AEM 6.5, not on AEM as a Cloud Service. Adobe recommends Dynamic Media with OpenAPI over the older Connected Assets.
aemsites-aemassets.gain: Your authors place brand-approved images from the DAM onto pages built with the Image v3 and Teaser v2 components. Other components need custom work. Changes to approved assets reach the live site without re-uploading.

aemassets-ajo.how: How AEM Assets is integrated with Journey Optimizer depends on your Adobe contract. Your marketers pick assets from an Assets as a Cloud Service repository in the Email Designer. If you have Dynamic Media with OpenAPI enabled, approved renditions stay current when assets change in AEM.
aemassets-ajo.gain: Your marketers place DAM images into email content. If you have Dynamic Media with OpenAPI enabled, approved renditions update in journey content when the asset changes in AEM.

commerce-aemsites.how: The Commerce Integration Framework (CIF) add-on, provisioned by Adobe, connects your AEM Sites as a Cloud Service to your Adobe Commerce GraphQL endpoint. Your authors can then search, browse and use product data inside AEM. It suits headless AEM content and existing CIF sites. Adobe recommends Edge Delivery with the Commerce Storefront for new storefronts, and documents a headless AEM storefront that starts with the CIF add-on. We confirm the storefront route with Adobe before this work starts.
commerce-aemsites.gain: Your authors find real products from the Commerce catalog while building headless content, and pages on existing CIF sites, so shopping content uses live product data instead of copied details.
commerce-aemsites.note: Adobe lists the CIF storefront and CIF Core Components as in maintenance mode, and recommends Edge Delivery with the Commerce Storefront for new storefronts. Confirm with Adobe before proposing new CIF storefront work for your client.

commerce-aemassets.how: The AEM Assets Integration for Commerce links your approved AEM Assets to Commerce products by SKU, or by custom matching built in Adobe Developer App Builder, and syncs them into your catalog. Your merchandisers can also pick DAM assets inside the Commerce Admin. On Commerce on Cloud and on-premises it is an Adobe extension we install. On Commerce as a Cloud Service we configure it in the Commerce Admin.
commerce-aemassets.gain: Your merchandisers manage product images once in AEM Assets. Approved images tagged with SKUs reach your Commerce products, most within five minutes, as Adobe documents. That keeps your storefronts accurate and on brand.

bv-cja.how: Brand Visibility sends aggregate AI-agent activity (from CDN logs, by URL and host) into CJA through an Experience Platform source. AI-referred visits and conversions come from CJA's own web data, and Brand Visibility reads those results for its business impact view.
bv-cja.gain: Four separate measures. Brand Visibility adds AI-agent activity (from CDN logs) and monitored visibility (tracked prompts); AI-referred visits and conversions come from your CJA web data. Any lift is measured with a test, not assumed. The data is aggregate: nothing ties a person to an AI mention.
bv-cja.note: The AI-referred visits and conversions come from the client's own CJA web data, which ordinary referrer reporting can show without Brand Visibility; lift comes only from a test. Keep that in mind when you pitch the integration's value.

rtcdp-bc.how: Concierge events land in Experience Platform datasets. The baseline is anonymous visitors. Profile context in replies needs Adobe to enable the integration for your tenant, use case and region, so we get Adobe's written confirmation before this work starts.
rtcdp-bc.gain: Agreed conversation data can inform audiences once the licensed collection, dataset and identity mapping are validated; answers that draw on a visitor's profile wait for Adobe's confirmation of the integration.
rtcdp-bc.note: Get Adobe's written confirmation that the Real-Time CDP integration is enabled for your client's tenant, use case and region before scoping profile context in replies, and do not assume the Brand Concierge-bundled dataset can be reused for other use cases.

aemsites-eds.how: Edge Delivery Services is part of AEM, and AEM Sites can be its content source: pages are managed in the Sites console, edited in the Universal Editor and published from AEM to Edge Delivery, and AEM Sites and Edge Delivery pages can share one domain.
aemsites-eds.gain: Your authors keep AEM Sites tools such as workflows, multi-site management, translation and launches (with the Universal Editor extensions enabled), your visitors get fast Edge Delivery pages, and both can run on one domain during a phased move with CDN routing rules.
aemsites-eds.note: When every page runs on Edge Delivery, take the Site build with components and templates service out on the AEM Sites card; the one-domain service sits under More services on this card.

commerce-ajo.how: Commerce events sent through Data Connection reach Journey Optimizer, which listens for them to start journeys such as abandoned cart.
commerce-ajo.gain: Abandoned carts and browses can start personalized email or push journeys; other channels need their own Journey Optimizer setup.
commerce-ajo.note: The Data Connection setup is priced once, as Commerce Data Connection to Platform on the Adobe Commerce + Real-Time CDP card. Adobe does not state availability for this route; confirm it with Adobe for your client's tenant.

commerce-cja.how: Commerce data sent through Data Connection lands in Experience Platform datasets that Customer Journey Analytics can analyze.
commerce-cja.gain: Store browsing, carts and orders sit next to any other datasets you add to the same CJA connection, so your teams can analyze purchase paths across channels.
commerce-cja.note: The Data Connection setup is priced once, as Commerce Data Connection to Platform on the Adobe Commerce + Real-Time CDP card. Adobe does not state availability for this route; confirm it with Adobe for your client's tenant.

cstore-cja.how: An Experience Platform cloud storage source loads the files on a schedule into a dataset, which the CJA connection reads.
cstore-cja.gain: Data you already export to files, next to web and AI-referred traffic.

aemforms-aemsites.how: AEM Forms provides the Adaptive Forms Container and Adaptive Forms Embed components, so your authors create a form inside an AEM Sites page or Experience Fragment, or place an existing form there. The Forms Portal components list forms, saved drafts and submissions on your Sites pages.
aemforms-aemsites.gain: Your visitors fill in and submit forms without leaving the page, your authors manage those forms with the site's versioning, translation and multi-site tools, and a portal lists forms, saved drafts and past submissions.

aemforms-eds.how: With Edge Delivery Services for AEM Forms, your forms are authored in the Universal Editor (or in Google Sheets or Excel for simple forms), rendered on your Edge Delivery pages by the Adaptive Forms Block, and submitted to Adobe's Forms Submission Service or to AEM Publish.
aemforms-eds.gain: Your Edge Delivery pages carry adaptive forms that your authors build visually in the Universal Editor, and submissions can still reach workflows, the Form Data Model and the other AEM Forms submit actions through AEM Publish.

aemforms-rtcdp.how: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service has a connector to Experience Platform: your forms are built on Experience Platform XDM schemas, and each submission streams to an Experience Platform dataset, where Real-Time CDP uses it to update profiles.
aemforms-rtcdp.gain: What people enter in a form reaches Real-Time CDP by streaming, so your profiles and audiences include it without a custom integration, and your forms collect data in the same XDM fields as the rest of your data.

aemforms-marketo.how: A Marketo Engage cloud configuration in AEM gives your forms the Marketo data model, and the Submit to Marketo Engage action sends each submission to Marketo for processing.
aemforms-marketo.gain: Submissions from your adaptive forms land in the Marketo Engage People database, where your smart campaigns and follow-up emails can act on them, without a separate form data model.

aemforms-workfront.how: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service has a connector that submits an adaptive form to a Workfront Fusion scenario through a webhook. We build the scenario, which then acts on the data, for example by starting work in Workfront.
aemforms-workfront.gain: A submitted form starts a Fusion scenario that can create projects, assign tasks, send notifications and update statuses, so your intake does not wait for someone to re-key the request.

aemforms-cw.how: AEM's Forms Agentic Capability works through Coworker Chat: your users describe a form or a change in plain words, and it creates or updates the adaptive form in your AEM environment and returns an editor link. Adobe confirms that Coworker is available to your organization before this service starts.
aemforms-cw.gain: Your business users describe a form or a change in plain words and get an adaptive form to review in the editor, on Core Components or Edge Delivery, which leaves your developers the custom work.

rtcdp-collab.how: Real-Time CDP Collaboration links to your Real-Time CDP sandbox. It takes the audiences you choose, matched on hashed keys under your consent rules, and brings the audiences a collaborator shares with you back into Audience Portal.
rtcdp-collab.gain: Your audiences meet a publisher's or another brand's audiences without either side seeing the other's records. You see the overlap, and the audiences a collaborator sends you arrive in Real-Time CDP for you to activate and measure.

rtcdp-mmm.how: Marketing Campaign Analytics and Real-Time CDP both work on your Experience Platform data. The models use event data you already collect, and we read the touchpoint scores to find the customer segments that respond best and build them as audiences in Real-Time CDP.
rtcdp-mmm.gain: You see which customer segments respond best to marketing and reach more people like them with look-alike audiences in Real-Time CDP.

rtcdp-ca.how: Content Analytics reports inside Customer Journey Analytics. We build audiences there from the content and creative attributes people engaged with and publish them to your Real-Time Customer Profile, where Real-Time CDP activates them.
rtcdp-ca.gain: You group people by the content they responded to and reach them through your Real-Time CDP destinations and campaigns.

mmm-cja.how: Marketing Campaign Analytics saves its model and touchpoint scores as datasets in Experience Platform. We add those datasets to your Customer Journey Analytics connection, and the models reuse the event data Customer Journey Analytics already holds.
mmm-cja.gain: You analyze incremental touchpoint scores by segment and journey in Customer Journey Analytics, next to your conversion metrics.

cja-ca.how: Content Analytics is set up from inside Customer Journey Analytics. It adds content events and the attributes of your assets and pages to the connection and data views you choose, where they sit beside your behavioral and conversion data.
cja-ca.gain: You see which assets, pages and attributes lead to conversions and later journey steps, not only impressions and clicks.

ca-gspm.how: The ads we create and activate in GenStudio run in your Meta ad accounts. Content Analytics reads those accounts' ad data through Experience Platform and ties each creative, down to its attributes, to outcomes.
ca-gspm.gain: You learn which creative attributes work and put that into the next round of ads.

workfront-gspm.how: Workfront Proof takes over review and approval of the content created in GenStudio. Your approval templates set the stages and the reviewers, your reviewers comment and decide in the Workfront proofing viewer, and the decision shows in GenStudio before anything is published.
workfront-gspm.gain: Every generated ad and email passes your approval chain, with versions compared side by side and comments and decisions kept on record.

aemassets-gspm.how: GenStudio connects to your AEM Assets Content Hub repository. The assets you have approved there show up in GenStudio's Content library, where your creators choose them as the starting point for new ads and emails. GenStudio reads the repository and does not write to it.
aemassets-gspm.gain: Your creators build from the assets you have already approved, with no copies to download and upload.

ajo-gspm.how: An Adobe app connects GenStudio to your Journey Optimizer template library. Your authors choose a Journey Optimizer email template when they create an email in GenStudio, and your personalization fields stay as they are.
ajo-gspm.gain: Generated email content fits the templates you already send from, so it goes into your journeys without rebuilding.

marketo-gspm.how: An Adobe app connects GenStudio to your Marketo Engage templates. Your authors choose a Marketo email template when they create an email in GenStudio, and your Marketo tokens stay as they are.
marketo-gspm.gain: Generated email content fits the Marketo Engage templates you already send from.

rtcdp-gspm.how: Your Real-Time CDP audiences appear as a choice when your team creates content in GenStudio, once Adobe has brought the audience definitions in. The content is then written for that customer segment.
rtcdp-gspm.gain: Ads and emails are written for the customer segments you already target, alongside your personas.

cw-gspm.how: Coworker connects to GenStudio with each person's own sign-in and permissions. In a conversation your team asks how ads are performing, assembles a draft from a template or a recommendation and sends it for review, and publishes an approved ad to a connected channel.
cw-gspm.gain: Your team gets performance answers and first drafts by asking, and approvals still run through GenStudio's review.

ajo-xa.how: The Experimentation Accelerator lists the content experiments in your Journey Optimizer campaigns and journeys, adds AI insights and suggested next tests, and opens a suggestion you choose back in the campaign's Content Experimentation panel.
ajo-xa.gain: Your Journey Optimizer experiments sit in one view with lift and confidence. The accelerator suggests the next treatment to try, and we help your team turn the suggestions you accept into new tests.

ajob2b-aemassets.how: Journey Optimizer B2B Edition connects to your AEM Assets as a Cloud Service repository with service credentials, so your designers use images from your DAM in emails, templates and visual fragments through linked references.
ajob2b-aemassets.gain: Your designers pull images from AEM Assets into account journey emails. A change to an image in the DAM reaches live emails, and authors see which journeys use an image that was changed or deleted.

ca-cw.how: Coworker Chat answers your team's questions about content performance from your Content Analytics data. It runs each question against your Customer Journey Analytics data views that are configured for Content Analytics, with each person's own permissions.
ca-cw.gain: Your marketers ask which images, themes or messages drive engagement and revenue and get an analysis back, without building the report themselves. We set up the access and the prompts your team reuses.

xa-target.how: The Experimentation Accelerator lists the A/B activities from your Adobe Target organization beside your Journey Optimizer experiments. People with only a Target license open it from the Apps switcher.
xa-target.gain: Your Target tests appear in one view with their primary metric, lift and confidence, so your team reviews every test, and what it taught, in one place.

ajob2b-marketo.how: Your Journey Optimizer B2B Edition subscription runs on its own Marketo Engage instance for email delivery. We also connect your existing Marketo Engage instance, so account journeys add people to or remove them from Marketo lists and add them to request campaigns.
ajob2b-marketo.gain: Your account journeys hand people to the campaigns you already run in Marketo Engage, and your Marketo smart lists can leave out people who are in a buying group, so the two do not send over each other.

ajob2b-rtcdp.how: Journey Optimizer B2B Edition is built on Adobe Experience Platform with Real-Time CDP B2B. Your account and people audiences are built with Real-Time CDP account segmentation and activated when a journey is published, and journey and buying group data is written back to Experience Platform.
ajob2b-rtcdp.gain: Your journeys run on the accounts, people and opportunities already unified in Real-Time CDP. Audiences refresh once a day, and journey and buying group results come back to Experience Platform for your reporting.

ajob2b-target.how: An account journey adds people to an audience, and we activate that audience to Adobe Target through the Target destination in Real-Time CDP. The people your journey qualifies then appear as an audience in Target.
ajob2b-target.gain: The people a journey has qualified become a Target audience, so your website can show them the experience that matches where their account is in the journey.

express-aemassets.how: Your approved assets in AEM Assets open inside Adobe Express. Your teams search or browse them, place them in a design, and save the finished design back to AEM Assets with its folder and metadata.
express-aemassets.gain: Your teams build content from approved assets instead of downloaded copies, and finished designs return to your DAM, so it stays the one place for final content.

express-workfront.how: We attach your Workfront approval workflows to your Adobe Express templates. When someone makes a design from a template, it goes to a Workfront project for review, and it can be published only after your approvers decide.
express-workfront.gain: Your teams make their own on-brand content, and nothing goes out before the right people have approved it, with every comment and decision kept in Workfront.

express-frameio.how: Designs your teams make from Adobe Express templates go through your Workfront approval steps, and your reviewers comment and approve in the Frame.io viewer.
express-frameio.gain: Your reviewers use one tool for designs and video, and feedback stays in one place.

express-ajo.how: Your marketers open an image in Adobe Express from the Journey Optimizer Email Designer, edit it, and save it back for use in the email.
express-ajo.gain: Small image changes are made where the email is built, without a request to your design team.

express-marketo.how: Your Marketo Engage team opens an image in Adobe Express from Design Studio, edits it, and saves it back.
express-marketo.gain: One edit updates the image in every email that uses it, without a request to your design team.

express-ajob2b.how: Your B2B marketing team opens an image in Adobe Express from the Journey Optimizer B2B Edition asset repository, edits it, and saves it back.
express-ajob2b.gain: Image changes are made where your assets live, without a request to your design team.

express-gspm.how: The ad templates your designers build and lock in Adobe Express appear in GenStudio for Performance Marketing, where your marketers generate variants from them.
express-gspm.gain: Your designers control the layout once, and your marketers produce on-brand ads in every size without waiting for new templates.

express-creativecloud.how: Your designers' Photoshop and Illustrator files are placed in Adobe Express, either linked to the original so changes carry through, or converted into designs your teams can edit.
express-creativecloud.gain: Your designers keep their own tools, and the rest of your team reuses their work without asking for exports.

frameio-workfront.how: Your teams plan and track work in Workfront and review it in Frame.io. Approvals start in Workfront, your reviewers comment and decide in the Frame.io viewer, and access is managed once, in Workfront.
frameio-workfront.gain: Your project leads and your creative teams each stay in their own tool, files are not moved between systems, and every approval decision is recorded.

frameio-aemassets.how: When your reviewers approve work in Frame.io through Workfront, the approved files are sent to AEM Assets with their project details.
frameio-aemassets.gain: Finished work reaches your DAM with the right labels, without anyone downloading and uploading it again.

frameio-creativecloud.how: Your video editors share cuts for review and read the comments inside Premiere Pro, connected to your Frame.io account.
frameio-creativecloud.gain: Review feedback reaches your editors where they work, which shortens each round of changes.

creativecloud-aemassets.how: Your designers open, edit and save files in AEM Assets from a panel inside Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign. People who use other applications reach the same assets through a desktop app.
creativecloud-aemassets.gain: Your creative teams always work on the approved file and save new versions to your DAM, so local copies and broken links stop piling up.

creativecloud-workfront.how: Your designers see their Workfront assignments, comments and approvals inside their Creative Cloud apps, and open and save project files from a panel in Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.
creativecloud-workfront.gain: Your designers stay in the app they design in, and your Workfront projects always hold the latest version and its approval history.

planning-workfront.how: Your plans in Workfront Planning, such as campaigns, are linked to the Workfront projects that deliver them. A planned item can create its project automatically, and each plan shows the dates and status of its work.
planning-workfront.gain: Your leaders see plans and delivery together, and your teams stop entering the same campaign in two places.

planning-aemassets.how: Your plans in Workfront Planning are linked to the images, folders and content fragments in AEM Assets that belong to them, and your assets can carry details from the plan.
planning-aemassets.gain: Your teams see each campaign with its content, and assets are easier to find and reuse because they carry the campaign they were made for.

planning-gspm.how: Your campaigns, products and personas are managed in Workfront Planning and stay in step with GenStudio for Performance Marketing, so a change in one shows in the other.
planning-gspm.gain: You define each campaign, product and persona once, and the content you generate always matches your plan.

planning-cw.how: Your planners ask Coworker, inside Workfront, to find, create, update and link records in Workfront Planning. Coworker shows what it will do and waits for a yes, and every change is logged.
planning-cw.gain: Your team turns a brief into a plan faster and keeps records up to date with less manual entry, with a person approving each change.

aemassets-fireflycp.how: Your production workflows read source files from your AEM Assets repository and write the finished files back to the folders we agree with your DAM owner.
aemassets-fireflycp.gain: Your approved hero assets go into production straight from the DAM and the finished variants come back to it, named and tagged, with no batches downloaded and uploaded by hand.

workfront-fireflycp.how: Workfront Fusion scenarios call the Firefly and Photoshop APIs with the prompt, images and settings from your Workfront requests, and return the generated or edited files to the same work.
workfront-fireflycp.gain: A request in Workfront can start image generation or repeat Photoshop edits by itself and bring the result back to the task, so your team reviews work instead of running jobs.

fireflycp-frameio.how: Your production workflows take source files from Frame.io and send the finished files back to the Frame.io projects we agree with your review team.
fireflycp-frameio.gain: Batches of finished variants arrive where your reviewers already comment and approve, with no files passed around in shared folders.

creativecloud-fireflycp.how: Your designers prepare InDesign and Photoshop templates with merge fields and tagged layers, and your production workflows fill them with copy, prices and images on every run.
creativecloud-fireflycp.gain: A layout is designed once and produced for every market, product and offer, so variants stay on the approved design and designers spend their time on the template, not the copies.

fireflycp-fireflycm.how: We share your trained custom models with the API project and pass each model's ID in the image generation calls your automation makes.
fireflycp-fireflycm.gain: Images generated in volume keep the products, characters and style your brand team trained the models on.

express-fireflycm.how: We publish your approved custom models and share them with the people and groups who design in Adobe Express, with permission to generate only.
express-fireflycm.gain: Your marketers generate images in your brand's own style inside Adobe Express, with a short prompt guide for each model.

creativecloud-fireflycm.how: We publish your approved custom models and share them with your design team, so the models appear in the Creative Cloud apps your designers work in.
creativecloud-fireflycm.gain: Your designers extend illustration sets, icons and photo styles in your brand's own look from inside their design apps.

ajo-fireflycm.how: We add your trained Firefly models to Journey Optimizer by their model IDs, so your marketers can choose them when generating images for emails and messages.
ajo-fireflycm.gain: Images generated for your campaigns in Journey Optimizer follow the style and subjects your own models were trained on.

workfront-brandintel.how: We set up AI Reviewers in Workfront that check each asset sent for approval against the brand rules Adobe Brand Intelligence has learned, and add them to your approval templates.
workfront-brandintel.gain: Every asset in review gets a brand check first, and your approvers see its comments beside their own review before they decide.

aa-target.how: Adobe Analytics becomes the reporting source for your Target activities. Target tells Analytics which activity and experience each visitor saw, and every Analytics metric and segment is available on the activity's report in both products.
aa-target.gain: Your testing team and your analysts read test results from the same data, and a metric or segment you did not choose before a test started is still available after it ends.

aa-rtcdp.how: A connector streams a copy of your Adobe Analytics report suite data into Adobe Experience Platform, where it builds customer profiles and audiences in Real-Time CDP. Your Analytics implementation and reports stay as they are.
aa-rtcdp.gain: The web and app behavior you already collect starts feeding profiles and audiences, with 13 months of history, and without new tagging on your site.

aa-cja.how: Your Adobe Analytics report suite data flows into Adobe Experience Platform and from there into Customer Journey Analytics, where it sits beside your other channels. Your Analytics projects and their segments and metrics can then be re-created in Customer Journey Analytics.
aa-cja.gain: You keep your Adobe Analytics reports running while the same data, with 13 months of history, becomes available for cross-channel analysis, and the projects your analysts rely on are re-created instead of rebuilt by hand.

aa-ajo.how: The web behavior you already capture in Adobe Analytics streams into Adobe Experience Platform, and Journey Optimizer listens for the events you choose, such as a cart addition, to start or advance a journey.
aa-ajo.gain: A cart addition, a search or a form start that you already track can start a follow-up journey, without tagging your site a second time.

aa-marketo.how: Marketo Web Personalization adds each visitor's organization, industry, segment and web campaign to your Adobe Analytics report suite, so that data shows in your Analytics reports.
aa-marketo.gain: Your analysts see which organizations and industries visit your site, what they read and which web campaigns convert them, inside the reports they already use.

aa-aemsites.how: Your AEM site is connected to an Adobe Analytics report suite, and a tags property with the Adobe Analytics extension sends page views and interactions from your pages to Analytics.
aa-aemsites.gain: Your pages report to Adobe Analytics from the first release, and your marketers change tracking in tags without a code release.

aa-aemassets.how: AEM Assets reads impressions and clicks for your images from an Adobe Analytics report suite and shows them as scores on each image and folder.
aa-aemassets.gain: Your content team sees how often each image is shown and clicked on your sites, and chooses, retires and relicenses assets on evidence.

aa-eds.how: A plugin from Adobe loads the Web SDK and tags on your Edge Delivery pages after they render and sends page views and events through a datastream to your Adobe Analytics report suite.
aa-eds.gain: Your Edge Delivery pages report to Adobe Analytics without giving up the page speed the site was built for.

aa-commerce.how: An Adobe Commerce extension sends your storefront events, such as product views, cart additions and orders, through a datastream to your Adobe Analytics report suite.
aa-commerce.gain: Your store's behavior shows up in the Adobe Analytics reports your business already reads, without hand-built tagging on each storefront page.

mmeasure-marketo.how: Marketo Measure connects to your Marketo Engage instance. It reads your people, program memberships and chosen activities, and turns them into touchpoints by rules we agree with you, with program costs and channels carried over.
mmeasure-marketo.gain: Your email, nurture and event programs get credit beside your paid and web channels, and people still in Marketo are attributed before they reach your CRM.

mmeasure-rtcdp.how: Your B2B data, such as accounts, opportunities, contacts, leads and campaigns, is brought into Experience Platform from your CRM and marketing systems and exported to Marketo Measure Ultimate, which attributes revenue across them.
mmeasure-rtcdp.gain: You attribute revenue across more than one CRM or marketing system, on the same data your Real-Time CDP uses.

mmeasure-aa.how: Marketo Measure shares account names, attributed revenue, funnel stage and open opportunities for your known web visitors with Adobe Analytics, where they can be used in segments and reports.
mmeasure-aa.gain: Your analysts segment site traffic by target account, funnel stage or revenue, and see which content engages the visitors who go on to buy.

acrobatsign-aemforms.how: Your forms in AEM Forms send the completed document to Acrobat Sign. Your signers receive it by email and sign in the order you set, and the signed copy and its status return to your process.
acrobatsign-aemforms.gain: Your applications finish with a signed document without printing or scanning, and your staff see who has signed and who has not.

acrobatsign-workfront.how: When a piece of work in Workfront needs a signature, the document is sent to Acrobat Sign automatically, and the task in Workfront updates when everyone has signed.
acrobatsign-workfront.gain: Your teams do not chase signatures by email, and your project record shows when each agreement was signed.

acrobatsign-marketo.how: Your agreement records flow from your CRM into Marketo Engage. Marketo Engage sends a reminder with the signing link when an agreement stays unsigned, and can tell signers when an agreement is on its way.
acrobatsign-marketo.gain: More of your agreements get signed without your sales team chasing each one.

acrobat-acrobatsign.how: Your staff send everyday documents for signature straight from Acrobat. Forms your teams prepare in Acrobat keep their fields when they become signing templates, and agreements can be generated from your data and sent for signature automatically.
acrobat-acrobatsign.gain: Everyone in your organization signs the same way, your regulated agreements get the extra controls they need, and fewer documents are prepared by hand.

acrobat-workfront.how: Your Workfront automations use Adobe's PDF services to create, convert, combine and read PDF files as part of a process, and the results are saved back to the work they belong to.
acrobat-workfront.gain: Your teams stop preparing routine documents by hand, and the documents attached to your projects arrive in the format the next step needs.

acrobat-aemsites.how: PDFs stored in your asset library open in Adobe's PDF viewer inside your web pages. Your authors choose how the viewer looks and whether visitors can download, print or annotate.
acrobat-aemsites.gain: Your visitors read documents without leaving the page, on any device.

acrobat-express.how: Your staff open a PDF in Adobe Express from inside Acrobat to restyle it, edit its images or start from a template, with your brand's colors, fonts and logos where your plan includes them.
acrobat-express.gain: Your everyday documents look finished and on brand without a design request.

acrobat-aa.how: The PDF viewer on your pages reports to Adobe Analytics when a document is opened, read, downloaded, printed or searched, and those events appear in your reports beside your other site data.
acrobat-aa.gain: You see which documents your visitors read and how far they get, so you know which ones are worth keeping up to date.
